questions.question: The point at which the entire mass of a system may be considered to be concentrated for the purpose of describing translational motion is called the
questions.explanation: The centre of mass is the point where the entire mass of a system may be considered concentrated for describing translational motion. The centre of gravity (A) is the point where weight acts and coincides with the centre of mass only in a uniform gravitational field.

questions.question: For a system of discrete particles, the position vector of the centre of mass is obtained by dividing the sum of the moments of mass by the
questions.explanation: The centre of mass is rCM = (Σmiri) ÷ M, where M is the total mass of the system.

questions.question: The centre of mass of a uniform thin rod lies
options: at one end of the rod
at the midpoint of the rod
questions.explanation: For a uniform thin rod, the mass is distributed symmetrically, so the centre of mass lies at the midpoint.

questions.question: For a homogeneous solid sphere, the centre of mass coincides with its
questions.explanation: A homogeneous solid sphere is spherically symmetric, so its centre of mass coincides with its geometric centre.

questions.question: Which statement is true about the centre of mass of a doughnut-shaped object?
options: It lies on the material of the object.
It lies at the centre of the hole.
It is undefined for such objects.
It lies on the outer edge.
questions.explanation: The mass of a doughnut (torus) is symmetrically distributed about its axis, so its centre of mass lies at the centre of the hole — a point not on the material itself.

questions.question: If the net external force acting on a system is zero, the centre of mass of the system
questions.explanation: By Newton's second law for the system, Fext = MaCM. Zero net external force gives zero acceleration, so the centre of mass moves with constant velocity (possibly zero).

questions.question: The motion of the centre of mass of a system is determined only by
options: the net external force acting on the system
the total kinetic energy of the system
the relative positions of the particles
questions.explanation: The centre of mass moves as if all external forces acted on the total mass there; internal forces cancel in pairs. So its motion is determined only by the net external force.

questions.question: When an external force acts on a system of particles, the centre of mass accelerates as if
options: the force were applied to the most massive particle
the entire mass were concentrated at that point
the force were distributed equally among all particles
questions.explanation: The centre of mass accelerates as if the entire mass of the system were concentrated there and the net external force acted on it (Fext = MaCM).

questions.question: In a uniform gravitational field, the centre of gravity of a body
options: always lies above the centre of mass
always lies below the centre of mass
coincides with the centre of mass
is independent of the mass distribution
questions.explanation: In a uniform gravitational field, the same g acts on every element, so the centre of gravity coincides with the centre of mass.

questions.question: The centre of gravity and the centre of mass of a body can differ when
options: the body is in free fall
questions.explanation: If the gravitational field is non-uniform (e.g. a very tall object), different parts of the body experience different g, so the centre of gravity no longer coincides with the centre of mass.

questions.question: For a system of two particles of unequal masses, the centre of mass lies
questions.explanation: The centre of mass is a mass-weighted average, so it lies on the line joining them and is closer to the heavier particle.

questions.question: The centre of mass of a uniform circular ring lies
options: on the circumference of the ring
at the centre of the ring
at a point outside the ring
at any point on the ring
questions.explanation: The mass of a uniform circular ring is symmetrically distributed about its centre, so the centre of mass lies at the centre of the ring (not on the material).

questions.question: Which of the following is true about the centre of mass of a system of particles?
options: It must coincide with one of the particles.
It always lies within the convex hull of the particles.
It is always at the geometric centre.
It depends on the choice of origin.
questions.explanation: The centre of mass is a mass-weighted average of positions, so it always lies within the convex hull of the particles. It need not coincide with a particle or be at the geometric centre.

questions.question: The position of the centre of mass of a system of particles is independent of
questions.explanation: The centre of mass is a physical point; its position is independent of the choice of coordinate origin. Its coordinates depend on masses and positions.

questions.question: For a continuous mass distribution, the sum in the centre of mass formula is replaced by
questions.explanation: For a continuous distribution, the discrete sum becomes an integral: rCM = (1 ÷ M)∫r dm.

questions.question: A non-uniform rod has a linear mass density that increases from one end to the other. Its centre of mass will be
questions.explanation: The centre of mass is a mass-weighted average, so it is closer to the denser end.

questions.question: In the method of negative mass, a hole in a uniform plate is treated as
options: a positive mass added to the plate
a negative mass subtracted from the plate
a separate object with its own centre of mass
questions.explanation: In the method of negative mass, a hole is treated as a negative mass subtracted from the full plate, which allows the centre of mass of the remaining portion to be found.

questions.question: A fisherman pulling a shark towards a boat is an example where the centre of mass of the shark-boat system
questions.explanation: The pull between the man and the shark is internal to the shark-boat system, so the centre of mass remains stationary (in the horizontal direction, neglecting external water drag).

questions.question: When a shell explodes in mid-air, the centre of mass of the fragments
options: follows the same parabolic path as before explosion
questions.explanation: An explosion is an internal event; the net external force (gravity) is unchanged, so the centre of mass follows the same parabolic path as before.

questions.question: Two blocks connected by a compressed spring are thrown into the air. At the highest point, the spring is released. The centre of mass of the system after release
options: continues on the original parabolic path
questions.explanation: Releasing the spring involves only internal forces, so the centre of mass continues on the original parabolic path under gravity alone.

questions.question: The velocity of the centre of mass of a system is given by the mass-weighted average of the
questions.explanation: vCM = (Σmivi) ÷ M, which is the mass-weighted average of the particles' velocities.

questions.question: The acceleration of the centre of mass of a system is equal to the net external force divided by
options: the total mass of the system
the mass of the heaviest particle
questions.explanation: Newton's second law for a system: aCM = Fext ÷ M, where M is the total mass.

questions.question: If the net external force on a system is zero, the acceleration of the centre of mass is
options: equal to the acceleration of the heaviest particle
equal to the sum of internal accelerations
questions.explanation: With Fext = 0, aCM = Fext ÷ M = zero — the centre of mass moves with constant velocity.

questions.question: Which of the following statements about internal forces is correct?
options: They can change the total momentum of the system.
They can change the motion of the centre of mass.
They cannot affect the motion of the centre of mass.
questions.explanation: Internal forces occur in equal and opposite pairs (Newton's third law) and cancel in the net force on the system, so they cannot affect the motion of the centre of mass.

questions.question: The centre of mass of a uniform rectangular plate lies
options: at the intersection of its diagonals
at the midpoint of one side
questions.explanation: For a uniform rectangular plate, symmetry gives the centre of mass at the intersection of its diagonals — the geometric centre.

questions.question: For a body with an axis of symmetry, the centre of mass must lie
options: at one end of the axis
questions.explanation: Reflection symmetry about an axis forces the centre of mass to lie on that axis.

questions.question: The centre of mass of a uniform solid cone lies
options: at the centre of its base
questions.explanation: By symmetry, the centre of mass of a uniform solid cone lies on its axis of symmetry, specifically at one quarter of the height from the base.

questions.question: A system consists of three particles of equal mass placed at the vertices of an equilateral triangle. The centre of mass is located at
options: the geometric centre of the triangle
questions.explanation: Three equal masses at the vertices of an equilateral triangle give a centre of mass at the geometric centre (centroid) of the triangle.

questions.question: The centre of mass of a system of particles can be located at a point where
questions.explanation: The centre of mass may lie in a region where there is no mass (e.g. the centre of a ring or a doughnut).

questions.question: When a high jumper arches over the bar, the centre of mass of the body
options: must also cross above the bar
always remains at the same height
questions.explanation: By arching, the high jumper arranges for the centre of mass to pass below the bar while parts of the body clear it — a classic Fosbury-flop technique.

questions.question: In a uniform gravitational field, the torque due to the weight of a body about any point is the same as if the entire weight acted at the
questions.explanation: In a uniform gravitational field, the total torque due to weight equals that of a single force Mg acting at the centre of mass.

questions.question: The centre of mass of an isolated system of particles moves with constant velocity because
questions.explanation: For an isolated system, the net external force is zero, so aCM = 0 and vCM is constant.

questions.question: If a man walks from one end of a boat to the other on still water, the centre of mass of the man-boat system
options: moves in the direction of the man's motion
moves opposite to the man's motion
questions.explanation: Walking involves only internal forces (man-boat), so the centre of mass remains stationary (neglecting water drag). The boat shifts in the opposite direction.

questions.question: The position vector of the centre of mass of a system of particles is defined as
options: the sum of the position vectors of all particles
the mass-weighted average of the position vectors
the average of the velocities of the particles
the sum of the masses times the velocities
questions.explanation: rCM = (Σmiri) ÷ M, which is the mass-weighted average of the position vectors.

questions.question: For a uniform thin rod of length L, the centre of mass is located at a distance from one end equal to
questions.explanation: For a uniform thin rod, the centre of mass lies at the midpoint, a distance L ÷ 2 from either end.

questions.question: Which of the following objects has its centre of mass outside its material?
questions.explanation: A uniform circular ring has its centre of mass at the geometric centre, which lies in the empty hole — outside the material of the ring.

questions.question: The centre of mass of a system of particles is a point that
options: moves as if all external forces act there
coincides with the centre of gravity in all cases
questions.explanation: By Newton's second law for a system, the centre of mass moves as if all external forces act there. It need not lie inside the material, and coincides with the centre of gravity only in a uniform field.

questions.question: When a uniform disk has a smaller disk removed from its edge, the centre of mass of the remaining portion
questions.explanation: Removing mass from one side shifts the centre of mass away from the hole — the remaining mass is biased toward the opposite side.

questions.question: The centre of gravity of an extended body is the point at which
options: the entire mass of the body is concentrated
the entire weight of the body may be considered to act
the body's kinetic energy is zero
questions.explanation: The centre of gravity is the point at which the entire weight of the body may be considered to act — the point about which the total torque due to gravity is zero.

questions.question: For a system of particles with total mass M and net external force F<sub>ext</sub>, the acceleration of the centre of mass is given by
questions.explanation: Newton's second law for a system: aCM = Fext ÷ M.
